Macrons

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Work & responsibility · Money, work & business

manage verb

run (a business, a household, money)

also run a business, administer, manage money, manage a household

classical

Cic. Inv. 1.25 (Lewis & Short): rem familiārem
Cic. Fam. 13.11 (Lewis & Short): negōtium alicujus
Traupman 343

administrō, administrāre, administrāvī, administrātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

manage, run, conduct

Lewis & Short: “to take charge of, to manage, guide, administer … (the most usual signif. of this word; very freq. in Cic. and the histt.)”. Traupman gives it for managing on a large scale.

Examples

  • quī sī ipse negōtium meum gererem, nihil gererem nisi cōnsiliō tuō

    For if I were managing my business myself, I would do nothing without your advice.Cic. Att. 13.3.1

  • ex quō nihil scīre potuī dē nostrīs domesticīs rēbus. dē quibus acerbissimē adflīctor quod quī eās dispēnsāvit neque adest istīc neque ubi terrārum sit sciō

    From it I could learn nothing about our household affairs; and they distress me bitterly, because the man who managed them is not there with you, and I do not know where in the world he is.Cic. Att. 11.1.1

  • Quis rem familiārem administrat? — Māter.

    Who manages the household money? — Mum.composed

Other words

  • cūrō, cūrāre, cūrāvī, cūrātum — see to, take charge of

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 4.13.7 (Lewis & Short): cūrāre omnia studiōsissimē ac dīligentissimē; Traupman 343

    Traupman’s first word for “manage”; see care, look after.

  • gerō, gerere, gessī, gestum — conduct, carry on (business, affairs)

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.3.1: sī ipse negōtium meum gererem

  • dispēnsō, dispēnsāre, dispēnsāvī, dispēnsātum — manage (household money and stores)

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 11.1.1: quī eās dispēnsāvit

    The word of the steward (dispēnsātor) who keeps the household accounts.

  • moderor, moderārī, moderātus sum — direct, run (a bank, a firm)

    verb, first conjugation, deponent; with an accusative or the dative · also used · classical · Traupman 164, 276, 343: argentāriam moderārī

    Classically to guide or govern, to keep within bounds (Lewis & Short); Traupman’s word for running a bank.

See also in charge, manage, care.
